The mighty ETU was front and centre at 50th ALP National Conference, and we won Sovereign Power!
 
At the conference, the ETU was proud to make the case for Sovereign Power, a plan to secure the future of Australian heavy industry through publicly owned renewable energy. As ETU National Secretary Michael Wright told delegates, it puts Australia on a path towards a prosperous future powered by sovereign energy and built around our national interests.
 
It was great to see the conference support Sovereign Power, and vote to put Sovereign Power into the ALP National Policy Platform – the document that instructs all ALP government policy.
 
Across the conference, ETU delegates made sure the voices of electrical workers were heard loud and clear, and without the work and power of ETU members, this win wouldn’t have been possible. 

UNION POWER.

The mighty ETU was in full flight at the National ALP Conference in Adelaide. We secured Sovereign Power in the party platform. This is a massive win for ETU members and a crucial point to get heavy industry powered up again - powered by publicly owned power - to keep building and making things in Australia.

ETU National Secretary Michael Wright addressed the conference, championing Sovereign Power and highlighting the need for publicly owned power in order to strengthen and to continue to build our country’s heavy manufacturing industries. 

This win is a culmination of years of hard work and advocacy by ETU members across the county, fighting for publicly owned power. 

The ETU will always fight for good, well-paid, secure, union jobs and Sovereign Power is a huge step to ensuring the energy transition puts electrical workers front and centre. 

Congratulations to all ETU members.

Union power. 

You can read more about Sovereign Power here - https://mckellinstitute.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Powering-Australias-Future.pdf

For generations, public power helped build Australia's heavy industry. Today, soaring energy costs are putting strategic industries and thousands of jobs at risk.

That's why we are calling on Labor's National Conference to back Sovereign Power, a plan for publicly owned renewable energy that delivers affordable, long-term electricity to the industries Australia depends on. This is about ending the industrial bailout cycle, protecting sovereign capability, and giving Australian manufacturing the secure energy it needs to thrive for decades to come.

The Labor Party comes from a place of democracy, and it is with these principles in mind that the ETU has been pushing for Sovereign Power at the conference. As Michael Wright said, if delegates embed Sovereign Power in the platform this year, it won’t be because the outcome was scripted. It will be because working people and their elected representatives made the case, mustered support and built momentum around the idea we need to deliver the future we want.

As investment in AI infrastructure accelerates, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to train the next generation of electricians. The ETU is calling for stronger apprenticeship requirements on major data centre projects to ensure these developments don't just deliver technology. They should be delivering tradespeople too.

As ETU National Secretary Michael Wright said, construction demand from data centres, renewable energy projects and large infrastructure projects like the Brisbane Olympics is placing enormous pressure on the industry's workforce. Without stronger apprentice ratios, we'll deepen the skills shortage instead of solving it.

Australia needs more electricians. Every major project should be training them.

To read the full article, visit: https://www.afr.com/politics/federal/labor-pressed-to-lock-in-apprentice-ratios-under-new-ai-standards-20260716-p60fxu

ETU QLD & NT members showed out to support AMWU and ETU WA Members in Port Hedland who are taking it to mining giant BHP, taking industrial action for the first time in decades. 

We rallied out the front of BHP’s Brisbane Head office to show that this blue will be fought all across Australia.

Union members at BHP Port Hedland deserve fair wages & conditions and Queensland & Northern Territory stands with you all in solidarity.

If you don’t fight. You lose! ✊⚡️

In June, ETU National Secretary Michael Wright joined Chief Economist at the McKell Institute, Alison Pennington, at the National Press Club in Canberra to launch Sovereign Power. 

As global supply shocks continue to put pressure on Australian industry and threaten hundreds of thousands of jobs, Australia has an opportunity to take control of its energy future. 

Sovereign Power proposes publicly owned renewable energy generation to deliver affordable, reliable power to strategic industries, strengthening our economy, protecting manufacturing, and creating secure jobs. 

Australia has done this before, and with Sovereign Power, we can do it again.

Find out more about why we need Sovereign Power here: https://mckellinstitute.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Powering-Australias-Future.pdf

Heard us talking about Sovereign Power? Here’s what it actually means: supporting manufacturing and heavy industry in Australia and protecting national interests through cheap energy. Slide to find out more about why and how Sovereign Power can save our heavy industry.

Australia's heavy industry is under pressure from rising energy costs. We've seen the warning signs at Tomago, Liberty Bell Bay, Whyalla and across the manufacturing sector. Rather than relying on endless bailouts, the Commonwealth should build and own renewable energy generation and provide reliable, affordable power to industries that are critical to Australia's national interest. By delivering energy at lower cost than the private market, Sovereign Power would strengthen Australian manufacturing, protect skilled jobs, and shield our economy from global energy price shocks. Visit https://www.etunational.asn.au/your-union-at-work/reports-submissions/ to find out more

On 3rd of June, ETU National Secretary Michael Wright and Chief Economist at the McKell Institute, Alison Pennington, travelled down to Canberra to deliver an address at the National Press Club. This speech from Michael launched Sovereign Power.

With global supply shocks hitting us hard and fast, Australian industry and hundreds of thousands of jobs are at risk, but there is an incredible opportunity before us.

We need publicly owned renewable generation, and Sovereign Power is just that. Australia has built and delivered electricity before, and we can do it again.

To find out more visit: https://www.etunational.asn.au/your-union-at-work/reports-submissions/

Our heavy industry has been struggling with the increased costs of energy. We’ve seen this at Tomago, Liberty Bell Bay, Whyalla and more. Without our heavy industry, Australia becomes reliant and dependant on foreign imports and manufacturing – a dependence that reduces our sovereignty. We need a plan to ensure that we can support heavy industry and manufacturing here in Australia, and Sovereign Power is that plan.

Instead of continuous bailouts for heavy industry, Sovereign Power is the idea that the Commonwealth can, and should, create and operate its own renewable energy sources. This energy can then be provided to industries deemed crucial to Australia’s national interests, such as heavy industry, for cheaper than the private sector is able to offer. The idea is simple, effective, and would protect Australia against the shocks of the international market.

To read our proposal about Powering Australia’s Future, visit: https://www.etunational.asn.au/your-union-at-work/reports-submissions/

AUSTRALIANS BACK SOVEREIGN POWER

Seven out of 10 Australians back government spending on renewable energy to power manufacturing facilities cheaply.

Instead of continuous bailouts for heavy industry manufacturing, the ETU is proposing that a Commonwealth agency be created to own and operate renewable energy and provide cheap power to heavy-industry, who keep citing high energy costs as their main source of financial woe.

A survey conducted by 89 Degrees East has found that roughly 3 quarters of Australians believe that governments should play a larger role in building and operating energy infrastructure. The survey polled around 4000 Australians.

To read more about the survey visit: https://www.perthnow.com.au/news/business/government-backed-clean-manufacturing-gets-public-tick-c-22432775

To read about the plan for Sovereign Power, visit: https://mckellinstitute.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Powering-Australias-Future.pdf
